title: Self-contained gate-elimination bound (2,1) for the MOD3-zero family

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"MOD3-zero family, defined in proof.md Section 1: L is the set of all binary strings x (including the empty string) whose number of 1-bits is divisible by 3. For every integer n>=0, f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1} is f_n(x)=1 iff x_1+...+x_n is congruent to 0 modulo 3 (so f_0=1). One fixed linear-time evaluator computes f_n at every length; the NP verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and f_|x|(x)=1, with witness bound W=0.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family (hence in NP with empty witnesses), C_B2(f_n)>=2n-6 for every integer n>=3 in the full Li\u2013Yang B2 model (all 16 binary gate types, unrestricted fan-out and depth, constant nodes free, every retained gate counted), with n=|x| the actual input length. Hence liminf over all integers n of C_B2(f_n)/n >= 2.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Lemma (unscored, proved in proof.md Sections 2-5): for every integer m>=3 and every residue a in {0,1,2}, every B2 circuit computing M_m^a(y)=[y_1+...+y_m congruent to a mod 3] has at least 2m-6 gates; and for m>=4 one bottom-gate elimination with a substitution y_i=0 removes at least two gates, giving C_B2(M_m^a)>=C_B2(M_{m-1}^a)+2.
